newsitem.title: JAPAN: IBJ says London branch made derivatives loss.
newsitem.headline: IBJ says London branch made derivatives loss.

text.p: Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) said on Thursday that its London branch made a 10 billion yen loss as of April 1 from derivatives trading.
The loss has been reported to U.K. authorities and to Japan's Ministry of Finance, an IBJ spokesman said.

The loss showed up in the accounts after the bank introduced a new mark-to-market accounting method from April 1, the spokesman said. The old method had effectively hidden losses on the London branch's positions in such derivatives as interest rate swaps.

The spokesman said there had been no wrongdoing and that the bank did not have any problems with risk management. He said the losses were on the branch's entire derivatives portfolio and did not result from any one individual transaction.

He said the loss had no effect on the bank's 1996/97 earnings to be announced on Monday because it was recorded in the company's books in April, after the start of the current fiscal year. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8570
